# Rules
- Packaged apps keep only Electron's en-US and ko locales; never en alone, which blanks the window.
- Settings rows read icon + label + control. Every string description sits behind its info glyph.
rulesTexts.big:
- Memory is ai-memory: `src/main/ai-memory/`, contract `src/shared/ai-memory.ts`, always on, no off switch (user's rule below). Settings › Memory (`settings/memory/MemorySection.tsx`) is the ONLY memory setting; its only switch-like control is the terminal omp button. Every UI string says just "Memory"/"메모리", never "ai-memory"; no link to the project's repo or docs, no credits in the UI. The licence notice lives only in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` and `LICENSES/`. Settings › Updates & about › This computer lists it as one of OMPdesk's own components (`settings/memory/MemoryComponentRow.tsx`: version, status, "updated with OMPdesk", no update control).
- **User's rule**: (1) Memory and learning are always on. The prefs `aiMemory`, `aiMemoryLearn`, `aiMemoryServiceOwned` are retired at startup (`retired-prefs.ts`; a stored `false` is ignored and deleted); `agent_power.set` has no `aiMemory`/`aiMemoryLearn` switch; no `AI_MEMORY_SET_ENABLED`. Delete all memory and per-page delete stay (they manage data, not the feature). (2) Only OMPdesk's own bundled, staged ai-memory build ever runs: never a PATH, `~/.local/bin`, Homebrew or Windows-script install; a foreign launchd unit or logon entry is replaced; a foreign wiring in the terminal omp is not adopted. (3) Updates come only with OMPdesk releases: nothing calls an `upgrade`, downloads an upstream asset or touches Homebrew, and the build has no `upgrade` command (Merging upstream); anything that replaced the staged copy is put back at the next launch because the staged copy is trusted only by bytes. Never add a path that updates, replaces or selects the memory binary or service from anywhere but the app's bundled build.
- Stock's `MemoryBackend` (`memory.backend` rows, the `memory` model role row via `HIDDEN_ROLE_IDS`, the bridge's `get_memory_report`/`memory_*` methods) is gone from OMPdesk. Stock itself keeps `memory.backend` `off` for RPC hosts (`protocolDefault: ["rpc", "acp"]`), so nothing is held as a runtime default.
- **No side panel view**: Memory lives on Settings › Memory alone (status, counts, pages by kind, handoffs, the web console); palette command `cmd.memory` ("Memory") opens it. No side panel glance (see Side panel).
- **OMPdesk's own source, built by OMPdesk** (ai-memory, MIT, [akitaonrails/ai-memory](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory)): it lives in `native/memory/` (a `git subtree add --squash` of an upstream tag; tag and commit in `native/memory/UPSTREAM.md` and `native/memory/ompdesk.json`; upstream `LICENSE` kept; `.github/`, `companions/`, `docker/`, `nix/`, `flake.*` and its AGENTS/CLAUDE files removed). Edit it like our code. No upstream release asset is downloaded or pinned anywhere.
  - `bun run build:memory` (`scripts/build-memory.ts`) runs the upstream release build (`cargo build --locked --release -p ai-memory-cli`, default features, committed Cargo.lock, `native/memory/rust-toolchain.toml` = 1.95) for the host (macOS arm64 or Windows x64). It writes the gitignored `resources/ai-memory-bin/<platform>-<arch>/ai-memory[.exe]` plus `ai-memory.build.json` (binary name, **SHA-256 recorded at build time**, version, upstream tag/commit, rustc, build time and duration). Each builder config ships that directory as `<resources>/ai-memory-bin/` outside the asar. `scripts/after-pack.cjs` `checkAiMemory` (and `packaging-config.test.ts`) fail a package without the binary and its record, with a version other than `native/memory/ompdesk.json`, or with bytes differing from the record. `scripts/mac-sign.cjs` signs the nested binary with the app's certificate; the release's `Verify bundle` verifies and runs it. Without Rust, `build:memory` prints how to install it and exits 1; the app then shows the failed phase "Memory is not built", never a crash (a dev run only reports).
  - CI: release.yml's `mac` and `win` jobs first restore the binary and its record (`actions/cache/restore`, path `resources/ai-memory-bin`, key `ai-memory-bin-<os>-<arch>-<hashFiles native/memory/** + scripts/build-memory.ts + resources/gui-bridge/memory-prompt.ts + resources/gui-bridge/redactor.ts>`). `memory-prompt.ts` and `redactor.ts` (`EMBEDDED_SOURCES` in build-memory.ts) are the inputs outside native/memory, because `install_hooks.rs` embeds them with `include_str!` into the omp extension it generates; a new outside input joins every key, `EMBEDDED_SOURCES` and ci.yml's change test. A hit runs only `bun run build:memory -- --check` (record matches `native/memory/ompdesk.json`, this OS/arch and the SHA-256 over the current `EMBEDDED_SOURCES` (`embeddedSha256`); the binary's SHA-256 is recomputed; its `--version` runs); after-pack and mac-sign.cjs check and sign as on a build. A miss installs Rust 1.95 (`dtolnay/rust-toolchain`), restores `Swatinem/rust-cache` (workspace `native/memory`, dependencies only), runs `bun run build:memory` and saves the cache right after the build so a later failing step keeps it. ci.yml's manual Windows jobs do the same; its `memory` job (macOS) builds only when `native/memory/**`, `scripts/build-memory.ts`, `resources/gui-bridge/memory-prompt.ts` or `resources/gui-bridge/redactor.ts` changed (then also `licenses:check`) and saves under the same key, so the next release hits the cache.
  - **Merging upstream**: `git subtree pull --prefix native/memory https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory <tag> --squash`. Delete again what we removed when it comes back (`.github/`, `companions/`, `docker/`, `nix/`, `flake.*`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) and the self-update: `crates/ai-memory-cli/src/commands/upgrade.rs`, `tests/suite/upgrade_e2e.rs`, `Command::Upgrade`/`UpgradeArgs`/`commands::upgrade` in `cli.rs`, `lib.rs`, `commands/mod.rs`, `agent_plugins.rs update_claude_code`, `install_hooks.rs restage_claude_code_scripts`, `install_layout.rs shipped_binary_name`, `Config.release_base_url` (`ai-memory upgrade` is an unknown command and nothing fetches upstream releases; `src/main/ai-memory/no-self-update.test.ts` fails when any of it comes back). Keep our own edits; update `UPSTREAM.md`, `ompdesk.json` and (if it moved) the version in `native/memory/Cargo.toml`. Then `bun run build:memory`, `bun scripts/gen-crate-notices.ts ai-memory && bun run gen:licenses` (`LICENSES/ai-memory-LICENSE` is the upstream MIT text; `LICENSES/ai-memory-dependencies.txt` lists every linked Rust crate and records the SHA-256 of `native/memory/Cargo.lock`; `licenses:check` fails when they differ), the packaged e2e and a release dry run. The binary updates only with OMPdesk (no CLI-tools updater entry). The upstream copyright and licence text appear only in `LICENSES/`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` and `native/memory/LICENSE`.
  - The launchd label `com.github.akitaonrails.ai-memory`, the Windows logon value `ai-memory` and the data dir are the binary's own and stay, so an existing install keeps working: a new build replaces the macOS binary in its one staged folder (Windows: a new `<version>-<hash>` folder the logon entry is re-pointed at), `setup` restarts the server on the new bytes, the data dir is untouched, other folders are pruned.

#### The Memory page

- Settings › Memory (`settings/memory/`; Settings sub-target `memory:<tab>`, the tab is the route). `MemorySection.tsx` is the shell: tabs Overview, Search, Pages, Handoffs, Sessions, Profile, Maintenance, one component each. Project selector `resolveProject` = the user's pick, else the project whose name ends with the active session's folder name, else the latest. An `unsupported` memory (no build for the platform, or a launch that does not set it up) shows only Overview.
  - **Overview**: status (the version alone while running; a badge names any other phase), the number of projects, or the project's name when there is only one (the project itself is the tab bar's picker, on Overview as on the other tabs except Profile), its counts, last capture (7-day activity and health in the tooltip), disk size, data folder, "Open web console" (`웹 화면 열기`, only while running) and its password, terminal omp, one privacy line (full text as tooltip). The web console is one row (`웹 화면`: Open, only while running, plus a key button that copies its password); terminal omp reads Use / Remove. List rows (Pages, Handoffs, Sessions, Search hits) are the kit `ListRow`: title first, statuses and the age (`TimeAgo`) in the right-hand column; omp, the only agent OMPdesk wires, is never named on a row or detail header (another agent is); internal ids (observation kinds, lint kinds, profile categories) read through `memory.*` labels.
  - **Search**: full text in the project or all projects (All projects is the first option of the tab bar's project picker on Search; no second scope control); a hit shows title, a two-line snippet, kind (the tier only where it is not the kind's usual one: semantic, procedural for a procedure, episodic for a session) and age, and opens in Pages, whose reader's meta line shows the page's path once (hits carry no tier or time on the wire; main fills them from the projects' page lists).
  - **Pages**: by kind (rules, decisions, gotchas, procedures, sessions folded, notes), markdown reader, Edit (a new version through the server's write path, keeping kind, tier, tags, pin), Pin, Helpful/Not helpful, Delete (confirm) and a **Deleted** group whose Restore reads the page from the checkpoint the delete returned (`AiMemoryDeleted.rev`, in `useMemoryPageStore.deleted` and the snapshot cache). Session pages are read-only.

indexes.text:
# Rules
- Packaged apps keep only Electron's en-US and ko locales; never en alone, which blanks the window.
- Settings rows read icon + label + control. Every string description sits behind its info glyph.

- Memory is ai-memory: `src/main/ai-memory/`, contract `src/shared/ai-memory.ts`, always on, no off switch (user's rule below). Settings › Memory (`settings/memory/MemorySection.tsx`) is the ONLY memory setting; its only switch-like control is the terminal omp button. Every UI string says just "Memory"/"메모리", never "ai-memory"; no link to the project's repo or docs, no credits in the UI. The licence notice lives only in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` and `LICENSES/`. Settings › Updates & about › This computer lists it as one of OMPdesk's own components (`settings/memory/MemoryComponentRow.tsx`: version, status, "updated with OMPdesk", no update control).
- **User's rule**: (1) Memory and learning are always on. The prefs `aiMemory`, `aiMemoryLearn`, `aiMemoryServiceOwned` are retired at startup (`retired-prefs.ts`; a stored `false` is ignored and deleted); `agent_power.set` has no `aiMemory`/`aiMemoryLearn` switch; no `AI_MEMORY_SET_ENABLED`. Delete all memory and per-page delete stay (they manage data, not the feature). (2) Only OMPdesk's own bundled, staged ai-memory build ever runs: never a PATH, `~/.local/bin`, Homebrew or Windows-script install; a foreign launchd unit or logon entry is replaced; a foreign wiring in the terminal omp is not adopted. (3) Updates come only with OMPdesk releases: nothing calls an `upgrade`, downloads an upstream asset or touches Homebrew, and the build has no `upgrade` command (Merging upstream); anything that replaced the staged copy is put back at the next launch because the staged copy is trusted only by bytes. Never add a path that updates, replaces or selects the memory binary or service from anywhere but the app's bundled build.
- Stock's `MemoryBackend` (`memory.backend` rows, the `memory` model role row via `HIDDEN_ROLE_IDS`, the bridge's `get_memory_report`/`memory_*` methods) is gone from OMPdesk. Stock itself keeps `memory.backend` `off` for RPC hosts (`protocolDefault: ["rpc", "acp"]`), so nothing is held as a runtime default.
- **No side panel view**: Memory lives on Settings › Memory alone (status, counts, pages by kind, handoffs, the web console); palette command `cmd.memory` ("Memory") opens it. No side panel glance (see Side panel).
- **OMPdesk's own source, built by OMPdesk** (ai-memory, MIT, [akitaonrails/ai-memory](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory)): it lives in `native/memory/` (a `git subtree add --squash` of an upstream tag; tag and commit in `native/memory/UPSTREAM.md` and `native/memory/ompdesk.json`; upstream `LICENSE` kept; `.github/`, `companions/`, `docker/`, `nix/`, `flake.*` and its AGENTS/CLAUDE files removed). Edit it like our code. No upstream release asset is downloaded or pinned anywhere.
  - `bun run build:memory` (`scripts/build-memory.ts`) runs the upstream release build (`cargo build --locked --release -p ai-memory-cli`, default features, committed Cargo.lock, `native/memory/rust-toolchain.toml` = 1.95) for the host (macOS arm64 or Windows x64). It writes the gitignored `resources/ai-memory-bin/<platform>-<arch>/ai-memory[.exe]` plus `ai-memory.build.json` (binary name, **SHA-256 recorded at build time**, version, upstream tag/commit, rustc, build time and duration). Each builder config ships that directory as `<resources>/ai-memory-bin/` outside the asar. `scripts/after-pack.cjs` `checkAiMemory` (and `packaging-config.test.ts`) fail a package without the binary and its record, with a version other than `native/memory/ompdesk.json`, or with bytes differing from the record. `scripts/mac-sign.cjs` signs the nested binary with the app's certificate; the release's `Verify bundle` verifies and runs it. Without Rust, `build:memory` prints how to install it and exits 1; the app then shows the failed phase "Memory is not built", never a crash (a dev run only reports).
  - CI: release.yml's `mac` and `win` jobs first restore the binary and its record (`actions/cache/restore`, path `resources/ai-memory-bin`, key `ai-memory-bin-<os>-<arch>-<hashFiles native/memory/** + scripts/build-memory.ts + resources/gui-bridge/memory-prompt.ts + resources/gui-bridge/redactor.ts>`). `memory-prompt.ts` and `redactor.ts` (`EMBEDDED_SOURCES` in build-memory.ts) are the inputs outside native/memory, because `install_hooks.rs` embeds them with `include_str!` into the omp extension it generates; a new outside input joins every key, `EMBEDDED_SOURCES` and ci.yml's change test. A hit runs only `bun run build:memory -- --check` (record matches `native/memory/ompdesk.json`, this OS/arch and the SHA-256 over the current `EMBEDDED_SOURCES` (`embeddedSha256`); the binary's SHA-256 is recomputed; its `--version` runs); after-pack and mac-sign.cjs check and sign as on a build. A miss installs Rust 1.95 (`dtolnay/rust-toolchain`), restores `Swatinem/rust-cache` (workspace `native/memory`, dependencies only), runs `bun run build:memory` and saves the cache right after the build so a later failing step keeps it. ci.yml's manual Windows jobs do the same; its `memory` job (macOS) builds only when `native/memory/**`, `scripts/build-memory.ts`, `resources/gui-bridge/memory-prompt.ts` or `resources/gui-bridge/redactor.ts` changed (then also `licenses:check`) and saves under the same key, so the next release hits the cache.
  - **Merging upstream**: `git subtree pull --prefix native/memory https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory <tag> --squash`. Delete again what we removed when it comes back (`.github/`, `companions/`, `docker/`, `nix/`, `flake.*`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) and the self-update: `crates/ai-memory-cli/src/commands/upgrade.rs`, `tests/suite/upgrade_e2e.rs`, `Command::Upgrade`/`UpgradeArgs`/`commands::upgrade` in `cli.rs`, `lib.rs`, `commands/mod.rs`, `agent_plugins.rs update_claude_code`, `install_hooks.rs restage_claude_code_scripts`, `install_layout.rs shipped_binary_name`, `Config.release_base_url` (`ai-memory upgrade` is an unknown command and nothing fetches upstream releases; `src/main/ai-memory/no-self-update.test.ts` fails when any of it comes back). Keep our own edits; update `UPSTREAM.md`, `ompdesk.json` and (if it moved) the version in `native/memory/Cargo.toml`. Then `bun run build:memory`, `bun scripts/gen-crate-notices.ts ai-memory && bun run gen:licenses` (`LICENSES/ai-memory-LICENSE` is the upstream MIT text; `LICENSES/ai-memory-dependencies.txt` lists every linked Rust crate and records the SHA-256 of `native/memory/Cargo.lock`; `licenses:check` fails when they differ), the packaged e2e and a release dry run. The binary updates only with OMPdesk (no CLI-tools updater entry). The upstream copyright and licence text appear only in `LICENSES/`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` and `native/memory/LICENSE`.
  - The launchd label `com.github.akitaonrails.ai-memory`, the Windows logon value `ai-memory` and the data dir are the binary's own and stay, so an existing install keeps working: a new build replaces the macOS binary in its one staged folder (Windows: a new `<version>-<hash>` folder the logon entry is re-pointed at), `setup` restarts the server on the new bytes, the data dir is untouched, other folders are pruned.

#### The Memory page

- Settings › Memory (`settings/memory/`; Settings sub-target `memory:<tab>`, the tab is the route). `MemorySection.tsx` is the shell: tabs Overview, Search, Pages, Handoffs, Sessions, Profile, Maintenance, one component each. Project selector `resolveProject` = the user's pick, else the project whose name ends with the active session's folder name, else the latest. An `unsupported` memory (no build for the platform, or a launch that does not set it up) shows only Overview.
  - **Overview**: status (the version alone while running; a badge names any other phase), the number of projects, or the project's name when there is only one (the project itself is the tab bar's picker, on Overview as on the other tabs except Profile), its counts, last capture (7-day activity and health in the tooltip), disk size, data folder, "Open web console" (`웹 화면 열기`, only while running) and its password, terminal omp, one privacy line (full text as tooltip). The web console is one row (`웹 화면`: Open, only while running, plus a key button that copies its password); terminal omp reads Use / Remove. List rows (Pages, Handoffs, Sessions, Search hits) are the kit `ListRow`: title first, statuses and the age (`TimeAgo`) in the right-hand column; omp, the only agent OMPdesk wires, is never named on a row or detail header (another agent is); internal ids (observation kinds, lint kinds, profile categories) read through `memory.*` labels.
